content_preview.title: Envoy 1.40.0 Makes HTTP/3 and QUIC Stable, Adds X25519MLKEM768 to Default TLS Curves and Moves the Build to Bzlmod
content_preview.summary: Envoy 1.40.0, published October 13, lists HTTP/3 and QUIC as stable, adds a hybrid post-quantum key exchange to default TLS curves and moves its build to bzlmod.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Envoy proxy project published version 1.40.0 on October 13, according to the [v1.40.0 release page](https://github.com/envoyproxy/envoy/releases/tag/v1.40.0). The release notes list HTTP/3 and QUIC as stable, add the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid key exchange to the default TLS curves, and move the project's build system from WORKSPACE to bzlmod. The release page also lists several breaking changes for people who build or embed Envoy.

editor_notes.content_quality: News piece, 887 words (range 400-1200). Clear structure (Overview, What Changed, Breaking Changes, Security Fixes and Backports, What We Don't Know, Analysis). Neutral, paraphrased throughout, no direct quotes, no AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: First-party sources only: all three sources are the official envoyproxy/envoy GitHub release pages (github.com is on the allowlist; no third-party coverage was used, which the article states in 'What We Don't Know'). Snapshots read from disk (source-0/1/2.html.gz; sha256 of decompressed content matches manifest; HTTP 200; suspicious_patterns null for all three). Because the snapshots are the full GitHub HTML pages, I also re-fetched the raw release bodies via the GitHub API (gh api repos/envoyproxy/envoy/releases/tags/<tag>) and checked every claim against the raw notes. source-0 (v1.40.0, published_at 2026-10-13T20:02:56Z, not prerelease/draft): CONFIRMED 'HTTP/3 and QUIC are now stable, including upstream HTTP/3 and all QUIC extensions'; QUIC listener mTLS, upstream QUIC client certs, P-384/P-521 ECDSA; X25519MLKEM768 added to default ECDH curves for upstream and downstream TLS incl. FIPS builds, revertible via envoy.reloadable_features.pqc_default_ecdh_curves; bzlmod switch, WORKSPACE removed, modules envoy/envoy_api/envoy-docs, MODULE.bazel migration with Envoy's custom registry alongside BCR; Clang/LLVM 18 to 22, --config=clang and clang-local removed, GCC via --config=gcc; Wasm engine flag and old --define flags failing the build; AWS-LC removal incl. --config=aws-lc-fips, ppc64le uses --config=openssl; mcp_router header forwarding (authorization) off by default with header_forwarding forward_all: true; Rust HttpFilter &self vs &mut self and the use-after-free note; route_specifiers, priority-group and dynamic-module route specifier; per_worker_subset, load_aware_locality (ORCA headroom), coalesced EDS LB rebuilds on by default; container-aware CPU detection (1.37 behaviour only with --cpuset-threads) ; event-driven drain; UDP hot-restart sessions; AI Protocol Manager (alpha) token usage for OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini as typed dynamic metadata; MCP filter items; access-log, OpenTelemetry (ext_authz/ext_proc client spans) and Prometheus native-histogram off-by-one fix; the 'family of races' after RDS update (AWS signing, composite, filter chain, local ratelimit, dynamic modules, SDS). Security section: the notes list 'URL normalization of path parameters (CVE-2026-73511/73551)' and 'HTTP/3 UAF (CVE-2026-73512)' as carried-forward 1.39.x fixes; article's ids match exactly. The article does not assign severities to any CVE (none are stated in the notes) and says only 'carries forward', so no unsupported severity or affected-version claim exists. source-1 (v1.39.4, published 2026-10-12T22:12:57Z): bug fixes for the route-config races (aws, composite, dynamic_modules, filter_chain, local_ratelimit, sds) and the stats fix 'introduced in 1.38.0 ... one bucket too low ... underreport quantiles' CONFIRMED; v1.39.4 lists no CVE, and the article assigns none to it. source-2 (v1.38.7, published 2026-10-12T20:39:07Z): 'Upstream security fixes: wasm: bumped wasmtime to 24.0.10 to resolve CVE-2026-54786' CONFIRMED (and present in snapshot, 4 hits); same histogram fix CONFIRMED. Dates: Oct 13 for 1.40.0 and Oct 12 for the patch releases ('the day before') CONFIRMED against API timestamps and snapshot datetime attributes. Minor nuance, not a correction: 1.38.7 omits the composite and filter_chain race fixes, and the article's wording attributes the race list to 1.39.4 and says 1.38.7 'carries the same histogram fix', which is accurate.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, identifier, flag name, version and date traced to the raw release notes. No fabricated specifics, no misattribution, no orphan URLs (body URLs equal article.sources). Headline, summary and lead are each directly supported. The 'stable' claim is phrased as 'release notes list/state', correctly attributed to the project's own notes.
